title: Evaluation of Test-Time Compute Constraints on Safety and Skill Large Reasoning Models
problem: Test-time compute scaling improves reasoning model performance through longer chain-of-thought sequences, but increases computational cost significantly. Need to understand trade-offs between compute efficiency and safety performance under resource constraints.
motivation: Reasoning models (o1, o3-style) generate long reasoning chains at inference time, enabling better performance but requiring more compute. Need strategies to optimize this trade-off, especially for safety-critical applications.
method: Two complementary approaches: (1) Fine-tune reasoning models using length-controlled policy optimization (LCPO) reinforcement learning to satisfy compute constraints; (2) Apply quantization to maximize CoT generation within compute budget. Evaluate safety performance under different constraints.
key_novelty: Study of compute constraints (length and quantization) on reasoning model safety; LCPO-based approach to enforce length constraints; systematic evaluation of efficiency-safety trade-offs.
contributions: Evaluation framework for test-time compute constraints on reasoning models
Length-controlled policy optimization (LCPO) via RL for enforcing reasoning length constraints
Quantization strategies for maximizing reasoning within compute budgets
Analysis of safety performance degradation under resource constraints
limitations: Abstract only; specific safety benchmarks not mentioned; unclear how LCPO training affects general reasoning capability; no performance numbers provided.
